title: The Mouse, the Frog, and the Hawk
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 青蛙把老鼠绑在脚上拖进水里，结果两个都被鹰抓走。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: A MOUSE, who had always lived on the land, and a Frog, who passed most of his time in the water, became friends.
paragraphs.zh: 一只一直生活在陆地上的老鼠，和一只大部分时间待在水里的青蛙成了朋友。

paragraphs.en: The Mouse showed the Frog his nest and everything he could think of that was pleasant to see; and the Frog invited the Mouse to go home with him and see all the beautiful things that are under the water.
paragraphs.zh: 老鼠带青蛙参观自己的窝，又把自己想得到的、所有好看的东西都指给他看；青蛙也邀请老鼠跟他回家，去看看水底下那些美丽的东西。

paragraphs.en: “No matter,” said the Frog; “I will tie your foot to my foot with a piece of this strong grass, and then I can pull you along nicely.” The Frog laughed as he said this. He thought it would be good fun for him, but he well knew that the Mouse would not enjoy it.
paragraphs.zh: “没关系，”青蛙说，“我用一根结实的草把你的脚绑在我的脚上，就能轻轻松松把你拉过去。”青蛙说这话时笑了。他觉得这对自己会是件好玩的事，可他很清楚老鼠并不会觉得有趣。

paragraphs.en: When the Frog had tied the Mouse’s foot to his own, they started together across the meadow. They soon came to the edge of the water, and the Frog jumped in, pulling the Mouse in with him.
paragraphs.zh: 青蛙把老鼠的脚绑在自己脚上之后，两人一起穿过草地。他们很快来到水边，青蛙跳了进去，把老鼠也一起拖了下去。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, how cool and nice the water is, after the dry, hot land!” said the Frog, as he swam gayly about. But the poor Mouse was frightened.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，离开又干又热的陆地，这水多凉爽、多舒服啊！”青蛙一边快活地游着，一边说。可可怜的老鼠吓坏了。

paragraphs.en: “Please let me go,” said he, “or I shall die.”
paragraphs.zh: “请放我走，”他说，“不然我会死的。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, never mind,” said the unkind Frog; “you will get used to the water. I just love it.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，别在意，”狠心的青蛙说，“你会习惯水里的。我就爱待在水里。”

paragraphs.en: But soon the poor Mouse was drowned, and floated up to the top of the water, while the Frog frisked about down below.
paragraphs.zh: 可是没过多久，可怜的老鼠就淹死了，浮到了水面上，而青蛙还在下面蹦来跳去。

paragraphs.en: Just then a Hawk saw the Mouse, and pounced upon it.
paragraphs.zh: 正在这时，一只鹰看见了老鼠，猛扑下来把他抓住。

paragraphs.en: As he flew away with it the Frog was dragged out of the water, too, for he was still tied to the Mouse.
paragraphs.zh: 鹰带着老鼠飞走时，青蛙也被拖出了水面，因为他仍然和老鼠绑在一起。

paragraphs.en: “Stop, stop!” cried the Frog. “Let me go. It is the Mouse you want.”
paragraphs.zh: “停下，停下！”青蛙叫道，“放了我。你要的是老鼠。”

paragraphs.en: “Come along,” said the Hawk; “I want you both. I will eat you first, for I like Frog meat even better than I do Mouse.”
paragraphs.zh: “一起走吧，”鹰说，“你们两个我都要。我先吃你，因为我喜欢青蛙肉，甚至胜过老鼠肉。”

paragraphs.en: In a few moments the Hawk had made a good supper, and there was nothing left of either the false Frog or the foolish Mouse.
paragraphs.zh: 没过多久，鹰就美美地饱餐了一顿，那只虚伪的青蛙和愚蠢的老鼠都没剩下一点。
